# Introduction


# Part 1 – Functional Analysis

## Rephrasing the requirements

Three features are a must for our application, they relate to the user experience and the different functionalities needed for an administrator to operate and manage cinema reservations. Those three features are as followed:

- As a customer, I can book a screening for an upcoming movie
- As an administrator, I can prepare the schedule of movie screenings
- As an administrator, I can see accounting details for a given period

First of all, this project must have two different sides: a customer side that will be the public and an administrator side. Accounts with the correct rights for the administrators are therefore required.

## Analysis of the features

For each features, here is the analysis of the requirements that need to be met in order to succesfully implement the feature.

### Book a screening for an upcoming movie:
We will need to implement a time management tool in order to classify movies as upcoming or ended. Many clients may want to book a ticket to the same screening at the same time, it is then essential for us to create a special status and management for unconfirmed bookings in order to prevent the oversale of tickets.
Booking implies the implementation of a payment and confirmation system.

### Prepare the schedule of movie screenings:
Given information about the movies that wished to be scheduled we will implement, without a front-end, a way to add movies to each room without there being overlaps between sessions. Information about movies will be taken via an API that will be from TMDB. With this information we will be able to recover the duration of the film and establish the time at which the screening will end.

### Accounting details:
Accounting details will be provided to administrators using the screening history and supplementary revenues from the other activities of the cinema. Graphs will be provided in order to have them be implemented later in the front-end by the other team.

Those three features mean, in technical terms, creating a backend that will be able to support a comprehensive frontend for customers to reach our cinema (that will be developed as a separate project). This can be translated by the existence of our personal API that will communicate information to the frontend of the application. It also means having a separate system dedicated for the administrators where the schedule can be made and information stored. Lastly, those features imply access to an external API in order to properly set schedules and have automatic and unique information about movies to present to the customers.
In order to use the limited requests of the TMDB API efficiently, we will establish a private database via POSTGRE SQL to store data about movies that will be screened. It will also be useful to track user actions (seen movies, posted comments…) in order to provide a more personal experience.

## Implementation of the features

### Priority features

Here are the features that are at the core of the application's design: 

#### User features:
For the customer, we will implement different features which will mainly be having access to the scheduled movies, seeing information about said movies, and being able to book a screening. An important part of this will be the query system that will allow the customer to search screenings by name of movie, genre, length, date and time of screening (maybe more).

The user will also be able to create an account to enjoy rating and writing comments about seen movies, have a friend list and be able to interact with them. It will be possible to establish one with an email address, pseudonym and password. Implementing this will mean having to implement a database corresponding to the movies seen by the user and a secure way to add them to the seen list to avoid review bombing on the future website.
Finally, a payment system will be implemented in order to have a fully functional back-end that will fit all the needs of our customer.

#### Admin specific features: 
Administrator accounts will be the same as user accounts, allowing them to also interact socially, but will have access to more features. Those features are mainly: establishing a schedule for the different rooms, being able to modify the pricing and also have the ability to check accounting details in order to run the cinema efficiently. 
Accounting details will not provide official documents but statistics about what the administrator would want to know. A search per time interval, movie and genre will be implemented.
A summary of the statistics we wish to implement:

- number of tickets sold
- turnover
- theatre occupancy rate
- sales per film
- sales per screening
- sales per day/week/month
- average ticket price

### API uses

#### Movie informations:
The list of scheduled movies being quite small and the potential userflow of the website quite high, we will import the movie data once on a personal database that will then be accessible without external constraints. TMDB’s API provides the summary in french and the french name of the movie.
Using an external API will allow us to provide the customer with all the information about any movie that the cinema will provide, for example its duration, actors, rating, trailer, box office, ratings and more.

#### Payment system:
We will implement a working payment system using Stripe. This method will allow us to implement a way to confirm bookings without having to worry about the privacy of the credit cards.

### Features included if time allows:
For the moment we do not plan to implement a system to let the customer choose their seats. This method is quite common and already in place at Bruz's cinema. However, if time allows, it would be a plus that would help us provide a better experience for motivated customers.

### Features excluded:
In this project, we will not allow the customers to cancel their bookings nor get a refund. We will also not send confirmation emails but rather provide the customer with a confirmation screen and access to its bookings.
We will not adapt our application for the specific use of adding more cinemas but rather focus solely on Bruz's cinema.

# Part 2 – Technical-Functional Layout

## Benchmark of the Movie Information API


Three movie data APIs are under consideration for the project: IMDb, OMDb, and TMDB. The goal is to compare them, rule out any unsuitable options, and select the one that provides the most relevant information based on the transmitted JSON (e.g., searching for information on the movie "The Odyssey").

# Comparison of the Three APIs {.unlisted .unnumbered}

| Criteria | OMDb | TMDB | IMDb |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Price | Free (1000 req./day) | Free (40 req./10s) or paid upon negotiation | Paid (AWS, min. $150,000) |
| Official Public API | Yes | Yes | No |
| Ease of Use | Easy | Easy | Difficult (AWS) |
| Data Completeness | Complete | Very complete | Very complete |
| License | Commercial use allowed | Non-commercial use by default | Mandatory commercial license |
| Language | English only | French supported (fr-FR) | French supported |

# Exclusion of IMDb {.unlisted .unnumbered}

IMDb ruled out:
No official public API available: access is provided via AWS with a minimum entry cost of $150,000. Incompatible with the our plan to build an app. The following evaluation therefore focuses solely on OMDb and TMDB.

# OMDb vs TMDB — JSON Comparison {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Based on the same search query ("The Odyssey"), here is the relevant data returned by each API:

| Data Field | OMDb (JSON) | TMDB (JSON, language=fr-FR) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Title | `"Title": "The Odyssey"`<br>*(English only)* | `"title": "L'Odyssée"`<br>*(Translated into French)* |
| Synopsis | `"Plot"` in English only<br>*"After the Trojan War..."* | `"overview"` translated into French<br>*"Vingt ans après son départ..."* |
| Genres | `"Genre": "Action, Adventure, Fantasy"`<br>*(English text)* | `"genres": [{"id_genre": "Aventure"}, ...]`<br>*(Translated)* |
| Runtime | `"Runtime": "172 min"` | `"runtime": 173`<br>*(minutes)* |
| Release Date | `"Released": "17 Jul 2026"` | `"release_date": "2026-07-15"` |
| Content Rating | `'Rated': 'R'`<br>*(US age rating classification)* | `"adult": False`<br>*(Indicates if the movie is rated adult/pornographic)*<br><br>`"softcore": False`<br>*(Specific flag designating non-explicit erotic content)* |

## Final Decision {.unlisted .unnumbered}

TMDB is selected: It is the only candidate among the two to return key fields such as title, synopsis, and genres translated into French (via the language=fr-FR parameter), whereas OMDb strictly provides these fields in English.


## Accounting Module 

The Accounting Module collects sales data and tracks financial performance. This report presents the main accounting and analytics features chosen for the system.

## Key Indicators {.unlisted .unnumbered}

* **Number of Tickets Sold:** Shows the total volume of sales. This number measures attendance and is used for official ticketing reports.
* **Total Revenue:** The total money collected over a chosen period. It helps monitor the general financial health of the cinema.
* **Hall Occupancy Rate:** The percentage of filled seats compared to the total capacity of the room. It shows how well each room and movie schedule performs.
* **Revenue by Movie:** Shows how much money each movie makes. This is useful to check movie profitability and calculate payments for distributors.
* **Revenue by Show:** Shows the earnings for each specific showtime (afternoon, evening, early screenings) to help improve the schedule.

## Time Tracking {.unlisted .unnumbered}

For both Total Revenue and Number of Tickets Sold, you can filter data by selecting a start date and an end date. You can also view results by day, week, or month with a graph to identify seasonal trends and follow performance over time.

# Part 3 – Technical Design

## Data model

Here is the data model of our databases:

\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=1\textwidth]{data_model.png}
\caption{Data model: structure of the application's database}
\label{fig:data_model}
\end{figure}

Each database contains an exclusive id, external ids and information that will need to be provided to the different users. "Movies watched" is only to keep track of the movies each user has watched and therefore will not be turned into a python object but rather a list of objects extracted from the database. 
"Pricing" and "Rooms" will allow administrators to change the pricings provided and information about new and existing rooms.

## Class diagram

Here is the class diagram of our application: [Class diagram](https://drive.google.com/file/d/141c9mCZy_gtnyeGRQAg4GBM6GtlaYw6n/view?usp=sharing)

The size of the diagram made it impossible to include it visually inside this analysis file without cropping out certain elements or impacting the readability of the text. 

The core idea is to separate the layers of activity to improve testability and separation of concerns. We thus have business objects which are modified and created via a dedicated service class that will communicate to a dedicated DAO class in order to access the database.

# Part 4 – Project management description

## Team organization

We are 4 people in the team and each one has a role for the whole project:

| Role | Person |
|---|---|
| Project Manager | Nolann |
| Technical Director | Simon |
| DAO Supervisor | Samuel |
| Testing Supervisor | Zoeb |

## Task assignment

We split the work mostly along these roles. Nolann handles coordination,
planning and keeping the Gantt diagram up to date. Simon takes care of the
technical side, meaning the architecture, the class diagram and the general
design choices. Samuel is more on the data side, so the database and the
data model, and how we access the data. And Zoeb is in charge of testing,
basically making sure stuff actually works before we call it done.

Of course this is not a strict separation: everyone can work on any part if
needed, especially since we're only 4 people. But these roles give each of
us a main area to focus on and to be responsible for.

## Methodology

We have a team meeting every week to check where everyone is, discuss
blocking points and decide what to do next. For now we mostly talk on
WhatsApp when we need to decide something quickly, and we put our documents
on Google Drive so everyone can access them. We know that WhatsApp is not the best communication tool for this sort of project work , so we're currently looking for a possibly more
efficient tool, but we haven't switched yet.

The code is on GitHub (github.com/nolannb35/ENSAI-2A-projet-info-team6), we
use it to keep track of the different parts of the project and work at the
same time without breaking each other's code.

We also want to do some kind of review before the big deadlines (Analysis
File, immersion, final delivery), just to check everyone's part actually
fits together before it's too late to fix.

# Conclusion

This first part of the project let us really understand what the Cinema
Club application needs to do, and turn a pretty vague subject into concrete
features we can actually build. We picked which parts we'll definitely do
(booking, scheduling, accounting stats) and which ones stay optional given
our November deadline, like the real payment provider.

We also got a first version of our technical design (data model, class
diagram, use case diagram, activity diagrams) and a clear plan with our two
Gantt charts. Some things are still open, like the exact database schema
details or a few edge cases in the booking flow, but we think we have
enough to start coding.

The next step is the development phase itself. We'll probably have to
adjust some of what's in this report along the way, but it gives us a solid
base to start from.
